title: JWST/NIRSpec and MIRI observations of an expanding, jet-driven bubble of warm H<SUB>2</SUB> in the radio galaxy 3C 326 N
question: How does AGN jet feedback affect the kinematics, heating, and star formation of warm molecular and ionised gas in the radio galaxy 3C 326 N, and can ro-vibrational H2 lines serve as a proxy for rotational H2 lines in turbulent environments?

data.sensitivity: RMS = 0.2 mJy bm^-1 in 15.4 MHz channels

what.value: Stellar CO band head absorption templates (specifically K4III star HD 9138)

evidence.quote: To model the CO band head absorption features, we used a template provided by Winge et al. (2009) instead of a Gaussian line profile.
We find that the template star of HD 9138, a K4III star, is a very good reproduction of our data without additional spectral types.

what.value: FIRST 1.4 GHz radio flux density of S_1.4 = 3.94 ± 0.14 mJy

evidence.quote: we compare the flux measured at 1.52 GHz, S 1.52 = 2.10 ± 0.09 mJy, with that of FIRST (Becker et al. 1995; White et al. 1997), S 1.4 = 3.94 ± 0.14 mJy

external_data.citation: Becker et al. (1995); White et al. (1997)

what.value: Star-formation rate (0.087 +0.106/-0.046 M_sun yr^-1), X-ray luminosity (10^40.63 erg s^-1), and dust mass (6.05 +0.376/-0.218 x 10^7 M_sun) from Herschel

evidence.quote: 3C 326 N has a very low starformation rate (SFR= 0.087 [+] − [0] 0 [.] . [106] 046 [M] [⊙] [yr] [−][1] [from] [Herschel] [dust] photometry; Lanz et al. 2016)
Lanz et al. (2016) estimated a dust mass of M dust = 6.05 [+] − [0] 0 [.] . [376] 218 [×][ 10] [7] [M] [⊙] [.]

what.value: Warm molecular gas mass (1.3-2.7 x 10^9 M_sun), warm ionised gas mass (2 x 10^7 M_sun), stellar mass (3 x 10^11 M_sun), and optical extinction (A_V = 0.17 mag)

evidence.quote: Ogle et al. (2007) and Nesvadba et al. (2010) estimated a mass of warm H 2 from the pure rotational line emission finding M H 2, rot = 1.1 × 10 [9] M ⊙ and M H 2, rot = 1.3 − 2.7 × 10 [9] M ⊙, respectively.
Nesvadba et al. (2010) also found M ion = 2 × 10 [7] M ⊙ for warm ionised gas probed by Hα.
Nesvadba et al. (2010) obtained a global estimate of A V = 0.17 mag from stellar population modelling in the optical

what.value: Spitzer/IRS warm H2 mass (1.1 x 10^9 M_sun) and [NeII] 12.82 um flux (4 x 10^-19 W m^-2)

evidence.quote: Ogle et al. (2007) and Nesvadba et al. (2010) estimated a mass of warm H 2 from the pure rotational line emission finding M H 2, rot = 1.1 × 10 [9] M ⊙ and M H 2, rot = 1.3 − 2.7 × 10 [9] M ⊙, respectively.

evidence.loc: 5.2. An extended, turbulent, multi-phase interstellar medium throughout the galaxy
evidence.quote: We can use the [NeII] flux measured by Ogle et al. (2007) of F([NeII]λ12.82)= 4 × 10 [−][19] W m [−][2]

recipe.goal: Derive ALMA continuum flux density and upper limit on CO(1-0) line flux and cold molecular gas mass
recipe.method: Measure nuclear continuum at 115.3 GHz rest-frame; compute 3-sigma upper limit on CO(1-0) integrated line flux from channel RMS using Sage et al. (2007) and Young et al. (2011) prescription; convert to L'_CO via Solomon et al. (1997) and to M_H2,CO via alpha_CO, then scale by area ratio
key_parameters: FWHM = 100 km s^-1, sampling = 43.26 km s^-1, N_b = 118, RMS = 0.2 mJy bm^-1
assumptions: alpha_CO = 4.3 M_sun / (K km s^-1 pc^2), and CO emission extends over the same area as warm molecular gas seen with NIRSpec (factor 5.3 larger than beam)

recipe.goal: Model JWST emission lines and stellar CO band head absorption
recipe.method: Spaxel-by-spaxel MCMC fitting of 1 or 2 Gaussians plus linear continuum for emission lines (selected by BIC), and convolved HD 9138 K4III stellar template plus 2nd order polynomial for CO band heads between 2.485 and 2.62 um
key_parameters: 5000 steps and 200 walkers (two runs) for emission lines; 2000 steps and 100 walkers for CO band heads
assumptions: Normal distribution of stellar velocities; instrumental line spread function accounted for

answer_key.quantity: ALMA 115.3 GHz rest-frame nuclear continuum flux density (S_115GHz)

evidence.quote: Continuum emission from the nucleus is well detected, with a flux density at 115.3 GHz in the rest-frame of S 115 GHz = 1.6 ± 0.01 mJy bm [−][1] .
Assuming a line width of FWHM=100 km s [−][1], a sampling of 43.26 km s [−][1] as in our data, and RMS = 0.2 mJy bm [−][1], we find σ line = 30.7 mJy km s [−][1] bm [−][1] .

answer_key.quantity: 3-sigma upper limit on cold molecular gas mass per beam

evidence.quote: we adopt the standard conversion factor appropriate for, e.g., the Milky Way, α CO = 4.3 M ⊙ / [K km s [−][1] pc [2] ] (e.g., Bolatto et al. 2013), and find a 3σ upper limit of 1.5 × 10 [8] M ⊙ bm [−][1] .

answer_key.quantity: 3-sigma upper limit on total cold molecular gas mass (M_H2,CO)

evidence.quote: Assuming that CO line emission would extend over the same area also seen with NIRSpec in warm molecular gas, we expect that the total molecular gas mass would be a factor 5.3 larger, i.e., correspond to a total of M H 2, CO = 8 × 10 [8] M ⊙ .

evidence.loc: 4.3. Continuum morphology and stellar absorption bands
evidence.quote: We find a systemic redshift of z syst = 0.08979 ± 0.0003, consistent with the value of z = 0.09 from Guillard et al. (2015) measured from [CII].

answer_key.quantity: FWHM of CO band head stellar velocity dispersion

evidence.loc: 4.3. Continuum morphology and stellar absorption bands
evidence.quote: From our CO modelling, we also find that the FWHM of the CO band head velocity dispersion is 5.1 ± 0.8 nm, equivalent to a velocity of 660 ± 100 km s [−][1] .

answer_key.quantity: Mass of very warm ro-vibrational H2 (M_H2,ro-vib)

evidence.quote: With these assumptions, and for an integrated H 2 1–0 S(1) line flux of 1.5×10 [−][18] W m [−][2], we find M H 2, ro − vib = 1.4×10 [4] M ⊙ .

answer_key.quantity: Maximum expansion velocity of bipolar bubble

evidence.quote: Extended line emission shows a bipolar bubble expanding through the molecular disk at velocities of up to 380 km s [−][1]

evidence.loc: 5.1. The nature of the emission-line regions in 3C 326 N
evidence.quote: We thus conclude that we are seeing an inflating, AGN-driven bubble expanding through the molecular gas, reaching an expansion velocity of up to 380 km s [−][1] .

answer_key.quantity: Average H2 0-0 / 1-0 line flux ratio across disk apertures

evidence.loc: 6. On using the H2 1–0 lines as proxy to the H2 0–0 lines in distant galaxies
evidence.quote: The average 0–0/1–0 ratio for all apertures in Fig. 11, not including the cavity or total source (blue and green apertures), is 5.5 ± 0.6.

answer_key.quantity: Radio core spectral index (alpha between 1.52 and 10.0 GHz)

evidence.quote: With the values for the radio flux and central frequencies given in Tab. 2.3, we find a α = 0.21 between 1.52 GHz and 10.0 GHz, a typical value for the flat-spectrum radio core of a radio AGN.

score_reason: For the ALMA component, the project code, beam size, channel width, RMS, and analytic upper-limit formulas are explicitly stated, though it is not stated whether archival image products were used as-is or re-imaged. For the primary JWST analysis, pipeline versions, MCMC priors, and walker setups are well documented, lacking only the exact aperture coordinates for regional tables.
rediscovery_reason: All datasets (JWST GO1-2162, ALMA 2015.1.01120.S, JVLA 18A-285) are public in archives, the mathematical recipe for the ALMA CO(1-0) upper limit and JWST MCMC fitting is explicitly given, and the main results are quantitative.
